input_signals.name: CheapImprovingProfitability
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(oiadp, at), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Value stocks whose operating profitability has been trending up over five years are cheap because expectations are anchored to stale weak fundamentals; the combination of low price and improving returns on assets marks expectation errors that resolve as the improvement becomes undeniable.
input_signals.reasoning: Here profitability enters as a dynamic state (slope of ROA) rather than a level, so the interaction identifies value traps versus recovering value instead of restating static quality. The multiplicative rank form ensures only cheap-and-improving firms score high, separating them from expensive turnarounds and cheap deteriorating firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( trend( ratio( oiadp, at ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: ExpensiveWeakMarginGlamour
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(RATIO(MUL(prcc_f, csho), sale)), IND_RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(oiadp, sale), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The short side of the profitability-value interaction is the sharper one: firms trading at high price-to-sales multiples while sustaining weak operating margins embed growth and margin-expansion expectations that their historical economics do not support, and they underperform as those expectations are revised down.
input_signals.reasoning: Price-to-sales is a valuation measure that is uninformative on its own because it mixes cheapness with margin structure; interacting it with realized three-year margins supplies the missing normalization and identifies genuinely overpriced firms. Deliberately targeting the expensive-plus-unprofitable corner tests whether the interaction's alpha is concentrated in the short leg rather than merely mirroring signal 1.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( mul( prcc_f, csho ), sale ) ), ind_rank( neg( ma( ratio( oiadp, sale ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WeakestLinkValueQuality
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Only firms that clear a high bar on both dimensions at once — durable operating profitability and a depressed price relative to book capital — represent fundamentals-versus-expectations mismatches; a firm that fails either test should be scored by its failing dimension, not compensated by strength elsewhere.
input_signals.reasoning: MIN is a strict conjunction and is not spanned by the average of the two ranks: unlike the product or the sum, it refuses to let extreme cheapness offset weak profitability (or vice versa), so its cross-sectional variation is orthogonal to an additive quality-plus-value composite in exactly the region where the two themes conflict. Using operating profitability scaled by assets rather than gross profits, and industry-relative ranks, keeps the profitability leg comparable across capital structures while the conjunction form supplies the genuine interaction content.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ProfitTiltedCashYield
input_signals.expression: MUL(RANK(RATIO(ADD(ib, dp), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_ZSCORE(MA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 3)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Cash-earnings yield should be rewarded when sustained operating profitability is above the industry norm and actively penalized when it is below, because a high yield on chronically weak economics reflects melting earnings and distress rather than undervaluation.
input_signals.reasoning: Replacing the degenerate 0/1 gate with a signed, continuous industry z-score removes the mass point and the perverse ordering: cheap-and-profitable firms score most positive, cheap-and-unprofitable firms score most negative, and firms with industry-average profitability sit in the middle regardless of yield. Ranking the valuation leg makes it robust to negative and fat-tailed earnings yields, so the sign flip comes only from the profitability channel, which is the economic content of the interaction.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( rank( ratio( add( ib, dp ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_zscore( ma( ratio( oibdp, at ), 3 ) ) )

input_signals.name: DeepValueTrapScreen
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Within the cheapest tercile on operating cash flow to price, the spread between operationally profitable firms and value traps is the dominant source of return dispersion; expensive firms carry no reliable signal and should be held neutral rather than shorted.
input_signals.reasoning: The gate is placed on the valuation leg and the graded score on the profitability leg, so the neutral (zero) group sits naturally at the center of a mean-zero industry z-score instead of being ranked above profitable firms, curing the breakpoint pathology of the earlier version. Cash-flow-to-price avoids the negative and near-zero enterprise-value outliers of a GP/EV construction, and operating profitability net of overhead (revt − cogs − xsga) is the discriminator most likely to separate genuine cheapness from decaying businesses.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.7 ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapWithStableProfits
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(VOL(RATIO(oibdp, at), 5))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Investors discount value stocks as a group for fundamental uncertainty, but the discount is applied indiscriminately: cheap firms whose operating profitability has been quiet and stable over five years carry far less genuine cash-flow risk than the cheap firms with erratic profits, so the stable ones are systematically over-discounted.
input_signals.reasoning: The graded channel is a second moment of profitability, not its level or its accrual composition, so it is neither Sloan accruals nor anything RMW measures — FF5 has no factor for profit-stream volatility. Because both legs sit inside the top-40% book-to-market group, HML exposure nets out and the surviving spread is the risk-versus-mispricing distinction inside value, which is exactly the geometry that produced FF5 alpha in gen 0.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( neg( vol( ratio( oibdp, at ), 5 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: EnterpriseYieldGateOperatingProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, ADD(MUL(prcc_f, csho), ADD(dltt, dlc)))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity-only cheapness confounds genuine undervaluation with financial leverage, so defining cheapness as operating earnings relative to total capitalization identifies firms whose whole enterprise is discounted; within that group, high operating profitability marks the ones whose discount is unwarranted.
input_signals.reasoning: This isolates a single design choice relative to Signal 1 — whether debt belongs in the valuation denominator — and directly tests whether the levered value traps that plague equity-based cheapness were diluting the earlier gates. Adding debt rather than subtracting cash keeps the denominator strictly positive, avoiding the sign-flipping enterprise-value outliers the critic flagged in gen 0.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, add( mul( prcc_f, csho ), add( dltt, dlc ) ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: CashYieldGateProfitPersistence
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oancf, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.7), IND_ZSCORE(TS_SUM(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oiadp, at)), 0.5), 5)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among firms cheap on cash-flow yield, undervaluation is distinguished from decline by how many of the past five years the firm ranked in the upper half of its industry on operating return on assets; repeated competitive standing shows the depressed price reflects sentiment rather than a broken business model.
input_signals.reasoning: The threshold is now applied to a cross-sectional industry rank at the median, matching the archive's INDICATOR convention, so the yearly flag splits the sample roughly in half and the five-year sum spans 0 to 5 with genuine dispersion instead of collapsing to a constant. Holding the winner's gate fixed makes this a direct level-versus-persistence test of what generated the only FF5 alpha in the archive.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( oancf, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.7 ), ind_zscore( ts_sum( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( oiadp, at ) ), 0.5 ), 5 ) ) )

input_signals.name: NetCashValueWithProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(RATIO(oiadp, at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: When a large fraction of market capitalization is covered by net cash on the balance sheet, the operating business is being valued at close to nothing; that is a bargain only if the operating business actually earns a return, because for a loss-maker the cash is a burn reserve rather than a store of value.
input_signals.reasoning: The valuation channel is balance-sheet liquidity value rather than any earnings- or book-based multiple, so its long-short spread is structurally different from HML and from every gate used so far in the archive. The interaction is essential rather than decorative: net-cash cheapness is famously contaminated by cash-burning firms, and profitability is exactly the variable that separates the two interpretations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( sub( che, add( dltt, dlc ) ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( ratio( oiadp, at ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapDeleveragingFromProfits
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(revt, cogs)), 2))))
input_signals.hypothesis: When a cheap firm devotes a meaningful share of its gross profit to retiring debt, value is transferred from creditors to equity holders while the equity multiple stays anchored to the pre-deleveraging risk perception; cheap firms that are instead adding debt relative to their profit base are financing decline and their discount is warranted.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the rejected operator swap with a new economic channel — capital-structure dynamics financed out of profits — that no archive signal touches, and it explains why value equities re-rate slowly: the equity claim's risk falls before the multiple responds. Scaling the change in debt by gross profit rather than by assets makes the measure an intensity of profit deployment with a strictly positive denominator, avoiding the sign instability that broke the gen-1 debt-coverage signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( revt, cogs ) ), 2 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: ClaimShareAndDebtFlowValue
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(SUMRANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), SUB(revt, cogs)), NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1), SUB(revt, cogs)), 2)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The stock of claims on gross profit and the direction in which those claims are moving are complementary pieces of information: a cheap firm with little of its profit pre-committed and which is additionally retiring debt out of that profit is transferring value to equity on both dimensions at once.
input_signals.reasoning: This fuses the archive's only signal strong on both metrics (CheapDeleveragingFromProfits, fmb 4.75 and alpha t 2.14) with the burden-level channel that supplies reliable alpha, and unlike gen 3's failed fusion both legs are continuous ratios sharing the same gross-profit denominator, so neither can dominate the ordering through discreteness. The economic content is the level and the flow of the same quantity, which is why averaging their ranks is coherent rather than arbitrary.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( sumrank( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), sub( revt, cogs ) ), neg( winsor( ratio( delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ), sub( revt, cogs ) ), 2 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: WeakestLinkCheapUnencumberedProfit
input_signals.expression: MIN(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), IND_RANK(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), dp), SUB(revt, cogs)), 2)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A firm is an attractive profitable-value proposition only if it clears a high bar on both dimensions simultaneously — a depressed price relative to book and gross profit that is not consumed by capital replacement — and failing either dimension should determine the score, because deep cheapness cannot compensate for profit that never reaches equity.
input_signals.reasoning: This preserves the interaction mandate the univariate yield abandoned while still removing the 60% mass point at zero that has flattened every gated signal's Fama-MacBeth slope, since MIN is continuous over the whole cross-section and is a strict conjunction not spanned by the average of its two ranks. Gen 0's MIN construction achieved fmb 4.15 but negative alpha because its second leg was RMW-like asset-scaled profitability; substituting the capital-consumption share, which the archive shows is FF5-orthogonal, targets both metrics at once.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), ind_rank( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), dp ), sub( revt, cogs ) ), 2 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapProfitFundedDisgorgement
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(dvc, 0), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), SUB(revt, cogs)), 2)))
input_signals.hypothesis: A cheap firm that uses its gross profit to hand cash out — paying dividends while simultaneously retiring debt — is demonstrating that the profit is real, unencumbered and under disciplined management, whereas a cheap firm absorbing new debt while distributing nothing is consuming outside capital to sustain itself and its discount is warranted.
input_signals.reasoning: This generalizes the archive's only two-metric success from debt repayment alone to total profit-funded disgorgement to all capital providers, which is the same economic flow measured more completely, and it keeps dividends in their coherent role as a distribution to equity rather than as a "burden". The flow construction is what supplied the FMB slope of 4.75, so the extension targets both metrics rather than adding another static claim-level ratio.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( coalesce( dvc, 0 ), delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ) ), sub( revt, cogs ) ), 2 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapClaimsPerRevenueDollar
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dp, xint), sale), 2))))
input_signals.hypothesis: The economic content of the claim-share mechanism is how heavily capital replacement and interest weigh on the business's scale of operations, and revenue is the correct scale measure because it is always positive; cheap firms carrying light fixed claims per dollar of revenue retain the flexibility to survive and re-rate.
input_signals.reasoning: This is the repair of the defect the critic identified across the whole burden family: with gross profit in the denominator, a firm with negative gross profit receives a spuriously *favorable* score, and such firms are common in the cheap gate, so part of the archived alphas may be driven by an inverted subsample. Substituting sales removes the inversion entirely while leaving the mechanism intact, so a comparison against EquityShareOfGrossProfitValue tells us how much of that alpha was real.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ratio( add( dp, xint ), sale ), 2 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapSelfFundedEquityBase
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(SUB(DELTA(ceq, 1), ib), COALESCE(dvc, 0)), sale), 2))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Book equity grows only through retained earnings or through external injection, so the residual after subtracting earnings and adding back dividends measures how much outside equity capital a firm consumed; among firms cheap on operating earnings, those funding themselves entirely from profits are undervalued, while those repeatedly absorbing outside equity at a low price are transferring value away from existing holders.
input_signals.reasoning: The clean-surplus residual is immune to the splits and stock dividends that contaminate raw share-count changes, which was the mechanical flaw in the previous version, and scaling by revenue removes the sign inversion of a gross-profit denominator. It is not the net-stock-issuance anomaly: the measure is a balance-sheet financing intensity relative to operating scale, evaluated only inside a cheapness gate defined on operating earnings, so it captures the reliance on outside capital rather than the issuance event itself.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ratio( add( sub( delta( ceq, 1 ), ib ), coalesce( dvc, 0 ) ), sale ), 2 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapEquityDearToCreditors
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(xint, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 2))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Equity and credit markets can disagree about the same firm: when the equity market demands a high operating earnings yield while the firm's own lenders accept a low interest rate, the better-informed creditors are contradicting the equity market's risk assessment, and the equity discount is the side that corrects.
input_signals.reasoning: Making the equity-market leg a gate rather than a subtracted term removes the arithmetic problem the critic identified — E/P dispersion swamping the borrowing-rate term — so the cross-sectional spread is generated entirely by the creditor-implied rate within a cheap universe, and the signal cannot collapse into plain E/P. Coverage is honestly limited to firms with debt outstanding, which is the economically correct domain because a firm with no borrowings has no creditor opinion to compare against.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ratio( xint, add( dltt, dlc ) ), 2 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapWithLongDatedObligations
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(dlc, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 2))))
input_signals.hypothesis: A cheap firm re-rates only if it survives long enough to do so, and survival depends less on how much debt it owes than on when that debt falls due; a high share of current maturities forces refinancing into exactly the weak market conditions that created the discount, while long-dated obligations buy the time for operating profit to be recognized.
input_signals.reasoning: Every claim measure in the archive concerns the size of obligations; this one concerns their timing, which is a genuinely new channel and one that FF5 cannot represent since neither HML nor RMW nor CMA contains maturity information. The ratio is bounded between zero and one by construction, so it needs no denominator repair and produces a stable, well-behaved cross-sectional spread inside the cheapness gate.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( neg( winsor( ratio( dlc, add( dltt, dlc ) ), 2 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapNetCashAccretion
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(DELTA(SUB(che, ADD(dltt, dlc)), 1), sale), 2)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The clearest evidence that a cheap firm's operations generate real surplus is the annual rate at which its net financial position improves — cash accumulating faster than borrowings — because that improvement can only come from operations, and it steadily converts a levered, risky equity claim into a safe one while the discount persists.
input_signals.reasoning: This is not the external-financing measure repackaged: a firm can raise no capital and repay no debt yet still accrete net cash, and conversely a firm can repay debt by drawing down cash with no change in net position, so the two constructions rank firms differently in exactly the cases that matter. It keeps the sales deflator that demonstrably improved slope and Sharpe, and it uses balance-sheet stocks rather than a dollar sum of the two archived flow legs.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( delta( sub( che, add( dltt, dlc ) ), 1 ), sale ), 2 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapClaimsMeetStableProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(oibdp, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(MUL(WINSOR(RATIO(ADD(dp, xint), sale), 2), WINSOR(VOL(RATIO(oibdp, sale), 5), 2)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Fixed claims are dangerous only in proportion to the variability of the profit that must cover them; a cheap firm with heavy capital-replacement and interest obligations and an erratic margin faces genuine ruin risk, whereas the same obligations against a stable margin are simply a financing arrangement and do not justify a discount.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive tested claim size (alpha 2.5%, dead slope) and profit stability (fmb 3.73, dead alpha) as separate additive channels; this multiplies them, which is the economically correct combination for a solvency risk that is the product of exposure and volatility, and it is the first construction that could inherit the slope from one channel and the alpha from the other. It replaces the flagged glamour mirror with a mechanism that FF5 cannot represent, since no factor contains a second moment of profitability.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( oibdp, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( neg( mul( winsor( ratio( add( dp, xint ), sale ), 2 ), winsor( vol( ratio( oibdp, sale ), 5 ), 2 ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapSelfFundedDistributableProfit
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), ADD(dp, xint)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), sale), 2)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The profit an equity holder in a cheap firm can actually count on is gross profit less what capital replacement and lenders take, less whatever new borrowing was required to keep the business running; when that residual is large relative to revenue, the discount is unjustified regardless of how the accounting earnings look.
input_signals.reasoning: The archive's two previous level-plus-flow fusions diluted (alpha 1.3% and 0.9%) because they averaged the *ranks* of two channels, letting each leg's noise offset the other; here the level and the flow are combined inside one accounting expression, so the composite is a single economic quantity — self-funded distributable profit — with one positive deflator. It targets the two ingredients that separately deliver the archive's best alpha (3.4%) and best slope (4.75).
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), add( dp, xint ) ), delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ) ), sale ), 2 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapPayoutPerOperatingCost
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(COALESCE(dvc, 0), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 2)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Among cheap firms, cash paid to shareholders net of new borrowing measures genuine surplus, and the right scale for that surplus is the firm's operating cost base — the recurring outlay the business must fund each year — because that is what determines whether the surplus is material to the enterprise.
input_signals.reasoning: The gate is now held identical to the archive's top signal (book-to-market at 0.6) so the test is unconfounded: exactly one element changes, the deflator, which is the repair whose importance the level family already demonstrated when gross profit was replaced and fmb rose from 1.13 to 2.83. Total operating cost is strictly positive for every operating firm, which eliminates the inversion whereby negative-gross-profit firms receive favourable scores, and it is an economically meaningful scale rather than an arbitrary positive number.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( ceq, mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), ind_zscore( winsor( ratio( sub( coalesce( dvc, 0 ), delta( add( dltt, dlc ), 1 ) ), add( cogs, xsga ) ), 2 ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapLeveredWithNearTermMaturities
input_signals.expression: MUL(MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(revt, cogs), MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)), 0.3)), IND_ZSCORE(NEG(RATIO(dlc, ADD(dltt, dlc)))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Holding the amount of debt fixed, the share of it that matures within the year determines whether a cheap firm controls its own timetable; those funded long can let operating profit be recognized, while those with a large current tranche must refinance into the same adverse conditions that produced the discount.
input_signals.reasoning: The graded leg is now the pure maturity share, which contains no information about the size of borrowings, and the second indicator restricts scoring to firms above the 30th percentile of leverage so that companies with trivial debt balances — whose all-current micro-balances produced the instability the critic identified — are held at neutral rather than scored as maximum risk. This makes the construction match the stated timing mechanism exactly, and both conditions are economically necessary: maturity structure only matters when there is real debt and only pays when the equity is discounted.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( mul( indicator( ind_rank( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), mul( prcc_f, csho ) ) ), 0.6 ), indicator( ind_rank( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ) ), 0.3 ) ), ind_zscore( neg( ratio( dlc, add( dltt, dlc ) ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: CheapTotalCapitalDisgorgement
input_signals.expression: MUL(INDICATOR(IND_RANK(RATIO(ceq, MUL(prcc_f, csho))), 0.6), IND_ZSCORE(WINSOR(RATIO(SUB(SUB(ib, DELTA(ceq, 1)), DELTA(ADD(dltt, dlc), 1)), ADD(cogs, xsga)), 2)))
input_signals.hypothesis: The complete measure of what a cheap firm returns to its capital providers is earnings less the growth in book equity — which captures dividends and repurchases together while netting out equity issuance — less any increase in debt; when that total is large, the firm is shrinking outside claims of every type out of current profit, and the equity holder's share compounds while the price stays depressed.
input_signals.reasoning: This replaces the published cash-holdings channel with the archive's most productive economic idea expressed completely: declared dividends alone (the archive's best signal) omit repurchases, which are the dominant distribution channel for most of the sample period, and the retained-earnings identity captures both without requiring split-contaminated share counts.
